sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Bijural federal state): federal public, criminal and tax law follow the common-law tradition, while private law in Quebec is governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991); Quebec limited partnerships are governed by CCQ arts. 2236-2266.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership)
CETA (EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement)
Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (1997, modernized in 2019)
Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) in force with 38+ treaty partners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (laundering proceeds of crime); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 38.1-38.4 (ultimate beneficiary disclosure to the confidential register segment; identity of general and limited partners is public in the register); Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2236-2266 (limited partnership constitution and commercial form); Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (partnership pass-through); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21; Canadian bank onboarding is performed under FINTRAC directives and Bank Act, S.C. 1991, c. 46 client identification requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Status of the corporate general partner (commandité)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority of the jurisdiction where the general partner is incorporated

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Partners evidencing all natural persons holding 25% or more of the limited partnership, directly or indirectly, and all authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, company secretary or notary public in the jurisdiction of the general partner and of each ultimate beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner (natural person) and of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the general partner, all limited partners, every natural person holding 25% or more, and all authorized signatories against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) Criminal Code anti-money-laundering provisions; (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, because the target payment rails (SWIFT wire transfers and documentary letters of credit under UCP 600) are predominantly USD-cleared; and (v) Revenu Quebec and Canada Revenue Agency flags where a non-resident general partner is present. PEP determination follows FINTRAC guidance and the PCMLTFR at SOR/2002-184, ss. 52-62: foreign heads of state, senior government officials, judges, senior military officers and their family members are treated as Foreign PEPs requiring enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval. Trade-based money-laundering red flags specific to green coffee container routing, including third-country transshipment, over-invoicing or under-invoicing of the green coffee, split shipments and requests for prepayment to non-producer accounts, must be escalated in the bank's and LC confirming bank's CDD process.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.industry_aml_risk_tier_assessment: Low_Risk_Standard for specialty green coffee bean import and container distribution, provided no cash transactions, no high-risk producer jurisdictions, and no third-party intermediary payment structures are used; any deviation from documentary LC or SWIFT wire rails elevates the tier to Medium_Risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises, online portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (name search, reservation and CLIC electronic filing services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, s. 63 and related regulations require that the firm name (raison sociale) of a Quebec limited partnership be expressed in French; a concurrent version in another language is permitted only if the French version is at least as prominent. The legal-form suffix must appear as 'societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in accordance with CCQ art. 2238. Only Latin-script transliteration is accepted; the Registraire will refuse names that are not distinctive, that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name or trademark, or that mislead as to the nature, quality or legal form of the enterprise (P-44.1, ss. 15-17).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Trust / Fiducie (requires prior approval of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions or appropriate financial regulator)
Insurance / Assurance / Courtier / Broker / Dealer (requires licensing or ministerial authorization)
University / Universite / College / Institut d'enseignement (reserved for recognized educational institutions)
Royal / Royale / Crown / Couronne / Canada / Quebec (implies governmental or sovereign affiliation and requires ministerial approval)
Inc. / Corporation / Ltd. / Ltee (misleading corporate suffixes for an unincorporated limited partnership)
Cooperative / Cooperative / Mutuelle (reserved for entities formed under cooperative statutes)
Foundation / Fondation / Association (creates a misleading impression of a legal person or charity)
Chamber of Commerce / Barreau / Ordre (professional or institutional monopolies), and any scandalous, obscene or public-order-offensive terms

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (Articles 2188-2200) and An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c P-44.1), together with the Partnership Act (Quebec) RLRQ c S-24, as applicable to limited partnerships
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a limited partnership in the Quebec enterprise registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement and may be deferred. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The general partner adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement as the foundational governance instrument. Capital contributions shall be as schedules require and may be deferred under the Act. The registered office is established at the address stated in the Declaration of Registration, being the address given in the mandatory enterprise filing. Officers are appointed as follows: the General Partner Representative, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Corporate Secretary, each authorized to complete the enterprise registration, open bank accounts, execute banking documents, and engage the registered agent. This resolution is effective immediately unless amended by written instrument of the general partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration name search and structural review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a compulsory name search to ensure the proposed limited partnership name is permissible and not confusingly similar. Review allowable suffixes for a limited partnership and verify the use of "S.E.C." or "Limited Partnership/L.P." is compliant with Quebec naming regulations.
required_dossiers: Statement of the general partner's name and jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a revised name declaration online or apply for a name authorization from the Registrar within 15 days; a formal complaint may be filed with the administrative tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the limited partnership agreement and statutory declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the written limited partnership agreement, stating contributions, profit-sharing, management authority of the general partner, and limitations on limited partners' participation. Execute a Declaration of Registration signed by the general partner, including the partnership's registered office address in Quebec.
required_dossiers: General partner's corporate documents (if corporate general partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is incomplete, the Registrar issues a notice of defect. Cure by filing an amended declaration within 10 days; no penalty if rectified timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - immatriculation department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration online or by mail with the prescribed fee. Include all mandatory information: partnership name, registered office, general partner's legal name and head office, and particulars of partners. Pay the registration fee using the official online payment module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar raises a query, the applicant receives a written notice specifying deficiencies. Submit an amended declaration with supporting documents within 20 days; the entry is deemed effective from the original date if cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and register with CRA/Revenu Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon enterprise registration, the Registrar issues a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Complete the CRA/Revenu Québec combined registration to obtain a federal business number (BN), GST/HST account, and QST account where annual worldwide gross nontaxable sales exceed $30,000. Register as an employer if applicable.
required_dossiers: Name and address of general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is rejected due to mismatch, file a query with Revenu Québec or CRA online. Provide corrected legal name and supporting certificate; the tax account may be backdated to the business inception date upon satisfactory correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure sector-specific import and food safety clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the importation of green (raw) coffee beans requires a Safe Food for Canadians Act import licence. Verify acceptable food grade origin and contamination controls. Register with the CFIA portal and obtain a signed import licence. Complete a customs importer code with the CBSA and have supporting documents ready for customs release.
required_dossiers: SFCR Import Licence application (e.g. valid for green coffee)
Commodity invoice and bill of lading
Certificate of origin where preferential tariff claimed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CFIA queries the application, provide additional traceability documentation and HACCP compliance evidence within 14 days. For customs issues, a correction under the Customs Act may be requested through the CBSA commercial clients portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for municipal business licence and occupational workplace compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing department of the registered office city and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the local general business permit in the municipality where the warehouse or registered office is located. If the limited partnership physically operates a warehouse, register with CNESST for employee health and safety, and obtain a CNESST establishment file for any workers. Maintain the fire safety certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal queries are cured by supplying missing zonal compliance. CNESST may require a conformity plan if the establishment file has deficiencies; a follow-up inspection can be requested.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) - Safe Food Import Licence division and Revenu Québec / municipal authority for commercial premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Import Licence (for green coffee storage/importing) and municipal general business licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Quebec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - wholesale distribution of green roasted coffee beans with no manufacturing or processing on site
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; minimal VOCs from green bean storage below threshold limits; hazardous waste management must comply with Quebec Regulation respecting hazardous materials (Q-2, r.35.2) if any pest or fumigation residues are generated. All waste shall be handled by a licensed carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the warehouse and office premises issued by the competent municipal fire service; structural load inspection confirming floor load capacity for palletized green coffee; CNESST employer registration and workplace safety clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec QST and provincial tax administration. Primary portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec CLIC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The non-resident limited partnership must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA before making a taxable supply in Canada. Apply via CRA's online Business Registration service or Form RC1. The GST/HST account is established as part of the BN. For Quebec supplies, register separately for QST with Revenu Québec through the CLIC portal, providing the partnership agreement, proof of foreign entity existence, and a designated Quebec or Canadian representative for service. Registration is compulsory once the partnership is no longer a small supplier; voluntary registration may be elected earlier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: For Canadian income tax purposes, a Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent; income, gains, losses, and credits flow through to partners. The partnership is, however, a registrant and a deemed person for GST/HST and QST purposes and must collect and remit indirect tax on taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election regime. The pass-through classification follows from the legal form of a limited partnership under Quebec civil law and the Income Tax Act. Available elections include: partnership fiscal-period elections under subsection 96(3), an election by a non-resident partner to file a Canadian tax return under subsection 216(4) instead of subjecting gross payments to Part XIII withholding, and GST/HST related elections such as a joint election on supplies of financial services between closely related persons. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act may apply to cross-border structures but do not allow reclassification of the partnership.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Multi-tier value-added tax: federal GST/HST at 5% in Quebec plus Quebec QST at 9.975%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in cumulative taxable supplies over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for both GST/HST and QST (small-supplier threshold); a non-resident partnership carrying on business in Canada must register once this threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system, digital stamping regime, or continuous transaction-control API mandate. Taxpayers must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST and QST registration numbers, the amount of tax payable, and vendor/purchaser identifiers. Electronic invoicing in EDI, PDF, or XML format is accepted if the original machine-readable data can be produced in legible form during audit. Records must be kept in Canada or be accessible electronically to CRA and Revenu Québec for a minimum of six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Green coffee beans are zero-rated as basic groceries under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when supplied in Canada and are also zero-rated as exported goods under Part V where the supplier exports them or delivers them to a carrier for export outside Canada. For QST, equivalent zero-rating applies to basic foodstuffs and qualifying exported goods. To claim the zero rate, the LP must prove that commercial possession of the coffee beans was transferred to a non-resident buyer or to the buyer's foreign carrier and that the goods were actually removed from Canada. Offshore services are not part of this goods-focused operation. Because green coffee beans are already zero-rated as basic groceries, export substantiation is still required to avoid potential reassessment if the supply is recharacterized as non-food-grade or if processing occurs before export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canadian International Trade Single Window or GCA portal
Commercial invoice describing single-origin specialty green Arabica coffee beans with HS classification 0901.11 or 0901.12
Packing list and container manifest indicating the foreign destination
Bill of Lading or ocean waybill showing the overseas consignee, port of loading in Canada, and port of discharge outside Canada
Buyer's payment release or inward remittance confirmation evidencing the flow of foreign currency proceeds
CBSA outward cargo control record or carrier's export declaration proving physical departure from Canada
Signed INCOTERMS delivery terms confirming transfer of risk to the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating for any supply not supported by contemporaneous export evidence. The consequence is reassessment at the full provincial and federal VAT rates of 14.975% plus interest. Misrepresentation or absence of reasonable care can trigger gross negligence penalties under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Tax Administration Act, a minimum 50% administrative penalty on improperly claimed rebates, and, for intentional fraud, criminal prosecution with fines or imprisonment. The normal reassessment period is four years, extending to ten years or indefinitely where a false statement or wilful default is established. Retrospective clawbacks may also revoke input tax credit entitlements and lead to denial of future zero-rating claims on subsequent export batches.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is functionally decentralized, with FINTRAC supervising anti-money laundering registration and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) handling import/export reporting alongside customs valuation concurrent with FX flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no exchange-control approvals, central bank registration thresholds, or blanket profit-remittance restrictions. Profit remittances may be effected freely through regulated financial institutions, subject only to FATCA/CRS reporting, anti-money-laundering verification, and standard transparency filings where a non-resident limited partner owns 25% or more of the partnership's income or capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Green coffee import proceeds and related export receipts may be retained in any major currency; the only statutory obligations are accurate record-keeping for income tax, GST/QST filing, CBSA valuation, and FINTRAC large transaction reporting where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for operating disbursements and FX execution, provided the EMI is a FINTRAC-registered money service business in Canada or a regulated EEA-EA fiduciary equivalent. Legal constraints include FINTRAC MSB registration, a Canadian agent or place of business for adequate supervision, and limitations on taking deposits. Capital contribution escrow, documentary letters of credit, and large commodity trade settlement are better served by Tier 1 Schedule I chartered banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance by general partners is not mandatory. Most Tier 1 banks permit fully remote onboarding with dual-step video verification, certified corporate registry extracts, and beneficial-ownership attestation from Revenu Québec or Corporations Canada. A registered office address in Quebec is required. Certain LC and credit facilities may require an in-person execution or notarized signing for the partnership resolution and authorized signatory list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident limited partners and low fixed capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement; Revenu Québec registration certificate; registered office proof; register of ultimate beneficial owners for every natural person holding at least 25% interest; source of wealth and source of funds statements; bank reference letters from home-country institution; undertaking to provide annual financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border green coffee counterparties located in emerging-market jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full KYC file on each supplier including business registration, trade license, phytosanitary export permits; commodity purchase contracts; commercial invoices; bills of lading or airway bills; certificate of origin issued by the exporting authority; insurance certificates and inspection reports for the shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Volumetric mismatch between projected specialty coffee turnover and partnership contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow projection; warehouse and freight contracts; take-or-pay sales agreements; past shipment records; audited or reviewed financial statements of significant trading partners; explanation of working-capital cycle and supplier advance structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity wire transfers to multiple overseas beneficiaries without local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual evidence of each trade leg; coherent disbursement matrix; value-chain description from origin farm to container distribution; proof of warehousing, roasting, or distribution relationships in Canada; employee and office documentation to establish substance at the Quebec address.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions should be routed by verified wire transfer using SWIFT MT103 from the home-country corporate or individual account to the LP's tier-1 Canadian operational account. Purpose code should reference 'capital contribution to limited partnership' or 'FDI-equity capital'; the payment narrative must mirror the partnership agreement capital schedule. Banks will likely file a FINTRAC Large Virtual Currency Transaction Report only when threshold applies; for CAD wire transfers over CAD 10,000, a Large Cash Transaction Report may be automatically logged. The partnership must record the injection as contributed capital, not revenue. No Bank of Canada approval is required. If a non-resident limited partner holds an interest of 25% or more, the entity must separately assess T106 reporting in Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound green coffee trade settlements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for open account or advance payments, and through documentary letters of credit governed by UCP600 for confirmed orders. The Canadian issuing bank will advise LC via MT700 to the supplier's bank and settle against compliant documents: commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and phytosanitary certificate. For payable transactions over CAD 10,000, the partnership must retain FINTRAC-compliant records. Disbursement narratives must clearly identify the underlying purchase order and shipment reference to facilitate bank AML review and avoid delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts in USD/CAD with tenors up to 12 months matched to import payment cycles
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies for supplier costs where local deliverability is restricted
Cross-currency swaps covering multi-year green coffee supply agreements involving USD, CAD, EUR, or other import currencies
Vanilla foreign exchange options used as price-insurance tools for upside protection on coffee price and conversion-rate volatility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Government of Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a calendar-year fiscal period ending 31 December, the declaration is due by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes a CAD 28 late charge plus interest; repeated or continued failure beyond 12 months exposes the registration to administrative radiation (strike-off) from the Registrar of Enterprises and loss of legal standing before Quebec courts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for calendar-year tax periods, on or before 31 May of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 24 per day (minimum CAD 100) up to 100 days, plus possible additional penalties of 10% of any unremitted partnership tax liabilities; no administrative strike-off applies for this federal filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No unconditioned statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership by size, activity, revenue, or partner count; an independent audit may become mandatory if required by the partnership agreement, by unanimous consent of all partners, by a lender or by securities legislation applicable to any partner or voluntary registration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under IFRS if any partner is a reporting issuer or elects to use IFRS; otherwise private partnerships normally apply Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) as permitted under Canadian accounting rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration must be accompanied by a declaration confirming the partnership's register of individuals with significant control (ISC) is accurate and complete. Any transfer or allotment that causes a person to hold 25% or more of the partnership's capital must be recorded in the ISC register and reported to the Registraire des entreprises within the prescribed statutory update period; for Quebec public-law obligations this is generally within 30 days of the occurrence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Limited Partners (names, addresses, contributions, obligations)
Register of Capital Contributions and Withdrawal Obligations
Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions and partnership agreement amendments

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: LP is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act (Canada), s. 96; no entity-level tax. Corporate partners bear federal 15% general corporate rate plus Quebec 11.5% general corporate rate (combined 26.5%). Resident individual partners bear Quebec top marginal rate of 53.31% (2024).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for green coffee importers. Available incentives: (1) CCPC small business deduction (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 active business income of corporate partners); (2) partial stock-option deduction for individual partners; (3) input tax credits for GST (5%) and QST (9.5%) recoverable on imported green coffee warehousing and logistics inputs; (4) SR&ED ITC available, though generally immaterial to wholesale distribution. GAAR (ITA s. 245) restricts artificial loss creation.
